page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.r6.4xlarge is a memory-optimized cloud server instance belonging to the ecs.r6 family. Built on KVM hypervisor technology, this instance utilizes an x86_64 architecture powered by a dedicated Intel Xeon 8269CY processor running at a base clock frequency of 2.5 GHz. The hardware configuration features 16 dedicated vCPUs combined with 128.0 GB of system memory, providing a memory-to-vCPU allocation ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU core. This profile is engineered to accommodate memory-intensive workloads that demand substantial volatile RAM capacity per execution thread.

The instance includes a baseline network bandwidth of 5 Gbps to handle cluster communication and data transfer tasks. It includes zero discrete GPUs and features no local ephemeral storage, requiring reliance on external block storage volumes for persistent data retention. Operating without local storage eliminates disk-maintenance overheads on the host level, though remote network storage latencies must be factored into storage-bound application architectures. The dedicated CPU allocation ensures consistent processing capabilities without core-oversubscription risks.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the high memory density relative to core count allows organizations to host large in-memory footprints without paying for unnecessary compute capacity. The ecs.r6.4xlarge is appropriate for memory-heavy enterprise software, including relational databases, in-memory caching layers such as Redis or Memcached, real-time analytics engines, ETL processing pipelines, and enterprise application servers requiring high RAM capacity per virtual CPU core.
